purpose: Guide an AI system that composes or refactors LevelUpDiag-Koali code without causing architectural drift. This contract complements the existing Markdown documents; it does not replace them.
precedence: the user's most recent explicit instruction
existing code when it does not contradict the three preceding levels of authority

rules: Create a file only if it appears in final_repository_layout or the user explicitly requests it.
Do not create a generic framework, plugin system, service, daemon, database, or network API.
Do not move a responsibility out of its owning module without a demonstrable need.
Prefer a simple function over a new abstraction.
Prefer the Python standard library.
Do not turn LevelUpDiag-Koali into a kOA-Linux component.
Do not reimplement a kOA-Linux validator inside the appendix; call it as an external process.
Do not treat the absence of an error as PASS when no final result was produced.

frozen_product_decisions.type: standalone development, diagnostic, and validation appendix
primary_job: align a series of Python .py/.pyw levels
frozen_product_decisions.gui: optional Tkinter/pyw facade over the same core as the CLI
frozen_product_decisions.portability_goal: core portable across Windows/Linux/macOS when this does not complicate the architecture

explicitly_forbidden_features: arbitrary code loading through entry points
automatic modification of the kOA-Linux checkout
shell=True in the normal execution path of a check
interpreting a required check without a result as PASS

definitions.Level: Unit declared in the manifest and independently executable.
definitions.Finding: Structured observation associated with a Result.
definitions.Artifact: Auxiliary file produced or referenced by a Run.
definitions.Campaign: Simple grouping of Runs against the same target.

semantics.PASS: The diagnostic was executed and the expected condition is satisfied.
semantics.FAIL: The target was tested and the expected condition is not satisfied.
semantics.SKIP: Execution intentionally omitted with an explicit reason.
semantics.BLOCKED: The expected diagnostic cannot be executed because of a prerequisite.
semantics.PARTIAL: Only part of the diagnostic is usable.
semantics.ERROR: Internal error in the level or LevelUpDiag code.

campaign_aggregation.WARN: WARN unless a FAIL/BLOCKED has higher precedence

frozen_rules: files relative to the appendix repository
an enabled=false level is not executed
a required=true level without a final result prevents campaign PASS

rules: example_path is safe to version and contains no secrets
local_path contains machine-specific paths and is not versioned
empty command = capability not configured; do not invent a command
target_repo_root must exist for levels N02-N10
control_dir and artifacts_dir are the only default LevelUpDiag write roots

finding_shape.severity: one of allowed verdicts or INFO

artifact_shape.path: relative path under configured artifacts root
artifact_shape.label: optional string

rules: result.json is the canonical conclusion of a Run
output.log contains execution details
output_tail is bounded and intended for the UI
timestamps are ISO-8601

campaign_contract.purpose: Simply group multiple runs; no policy engine.

fields.name: required string
fields.results: map level id -> result path or compact result

rules: a campaign does not change the semantics of a level
the selected level list is recorded before execution
a selected required level without a final result blocks global PASS
runtime root is ignored by Git
a new run does not overwrite history
latest may be copied or replaced atomically
no runtime data is required to start the repository

common_pattern: Each level is a thin file.
Each level loads AppConfig through load_config().
Each level uses run_cmd() for external commands.
Each level writes exactly one final LevelResult.
Each level can be launched standalone.
Local GUI logic for a level remains optional and does not change the verdict.
A level never directly calls another level file.

empty_command_behavior.required_level: CONFIG_ERROR if command is contractually required for that deployment; otherwise BLOCKED
empty_command_behavior.optional_level: SKIP or BLOCKED with explicit finding; never invent a command

allowed_interaction: read Git revision/status if git is available
forbidden_interaction: import internal koa Python modules to bypass public runners
cleanup or reset the target worktree
create files in target except outputs explicitly produced by the public koa command itself
koa_integration_contract.missing_public_command: BLOCKED or CONFIG_ERROR; do not synthesize a replacement implementation

delivery_exclusion_contract.goal: Verify that the appendix is absent from the provided staging or delivery artifact.
rules: inspection only; do not automatically delete residue
LevelUpDiag logs remain outside the deliverable
do not execute the contents of an inspected archive

pyproject_contract.build_system: setuptools or hatchling; choose one simple standard backend and do not add runtime framework dependencies

required_test_domains: N11 residue detection and clean case
test_style: tests must not require a real kOA-Linux checkout unless marked integration
use tmp_path and fake scripts for subprocess tests
no network required for unit tests

verification_before_code_is_considered_c: a synthetic PASS campaign produces summary.json and summary.txt
a synthetic missing-tool case produces BLOCKED or INFRA_ERROR, never PASS
a synthetic failing command produces FAIL
N11 detects an injected LevelUpDiag residue
N11 passes on a clean synthetic delivery tree
GUI imports and opens without executing a campaign automatically
ai_behavior_when_uncertain: Prefer the simplest implementation consistent with this contract.
Do not invent missing kOA commands; leave the command key empty and return a non-success explanatory result.
Do not add a new layer merely to make the design more generic.
When code and docs disagree, preserve the contract and update code toward it unless the user explicitly says otherwise.
When a change would alter a frozen decision, stop that change and surface the conflict in the implementation notes.
Do not create TODO placeholders for required final files unless the user asked for a scaffold-only pass.

code_complete_when: manifest exactly references the intended N00-N11 levels
verdict semantics are consistent across CLI, GUI, levels and reports
kOA access remains external and read-only by default
